title: Readme Studio config
description: Design of an animated GitHub profile README, rendered by the Readme Studio action.

kind.description: profile: the <login>/<login> README; project: a repository README

logo.description: icon id, or empty for a monogram

login.description: GitHub username the data is fetched for

options.description: Your name drawn on stroke by stroke, a typewriter cycling through your roles and an orbiting emblem.

typewriter.title: Typewriter roles
typewriter.description: Cycles through the roles from your profile.

greeting.title: Greeting line
greeting.description: Time-of-day greeting, date and moon phase.

options.description: A big typographic statement with a subline, brought to life by a gradient sweep, an outline draw-on, a letter-by-letter rise or a marquee.

corners.title: Corner marks
corners.description: Small registration ticks in the corners.

options.description: Your project's name drawn on, its tagline, version, install command and headline numbers over an ambient glow.

version.title: Version pill
version.description: Latest release tag next to the name.

install.title: Install command
install.description: Shown in a code pill under the tagline. Leave empty to hide. It also stays hidden while a placeholder it uses has no value, such as {npm} without an npm package in the Project tab. Placeholders: {npm} {repo} {project} {version}

emblem.title: Emblem icon
emblem.description: Defaults to the project logo; without one a monogram tile is drawn.

options.description: One animated, clickable pill per profile link. Each is its own image so every link works.
A shell session that types out commands about you, with live placeholders, syntax colours and a tmux-style status bar.

output.title: Output
output.description: One line per row. Colours: {a}accent {m}muted {s}string {n}number {b}bold {/}reset. Placeholders: {name} {login} {city} {company} {role} {year} {age} {days_alive} {account_age} {followers} {stars} {repos} {streak} {year_pct} {stack}. Wrap text in {? … ?} to hide it when a placeholder is empty.

status.title: Status text
status.description: Supports the same placeholders, plus {clock}, {time}, {date} and {tz}.

options.description: Your tools as a little solar system: up to three rings of brand icons orbiting a centre emblem.

legend.title: Ring legend
legend.description: Lists each ring's tools beside the orbit.

icons.title: Icons
icons.description: Icon ids such as typescript, react, docker. Inner rings hold fewer icons than outer ones.

options.description: A typographic introduction: monogram, name and pronouns, your roles, a short bio and chips for where you work and live.

bio.title: Bio
bio.description: Up to five lines; a blank line starts a new paragraph. Placeholders: {name} {login} {city} {company} {role} {year} {followers} {stars} {repos} {streak} {contributions} {project} {repo} {tagline} {version} {license} {forks} {contributors} {npm} {pypi} {crate} {owner}

monogram.title: Monogram
monogram.description: Your initials in an accent disc.

options.description: A tidy key-value list of things worth knowing about you, revealed row by row, in one or two columns.

leaders.title: Dotted leaders
leaders.description: A dotted line between each key and its value.

icon.title: Icon
icon.description: A brand icon, or a line glyph such as pin, briefcase, code, book, heart, rocket, globe.

options.description: A row of shields-style badges drawn right in the image, no third-party service, wrapping neatly across lines.

colors.title: Value colour
colors.description: Brand uses each icon's own colour; a per-badge colour always wins.

icon.title: Icon
icon.description: Brand icon or line glyph; leave empty for none.

options.description: Your strongest tools as filling bars, segmented blocks or radial gauges, each with its icon and level.
Experience and education on a vertical rail whose nodes light up one after another, with a live pulse on what you do now.

now.title: Live pulse on the first entry
now.description: Marks the top entry as what you are doing now.

options.description: A “let's work together” card with your availability, a short pitch and up to three call-to-action buttons.

ctas.title: Buttons
ctas.description: Buttons are drawn into the image; the whole card links to the URL below.

url.title: Link
url.description: mailto:, a booking page or any URL.

emblem.title: Emblem
emblem.description: Shown inside the signal on the right.

options.description: A live clock for your time zone that keeps ticking after the build, with your city, UTC offset and today's daylight band.

daylight.title: Daylight band
daylight.description: Approximate sunrise and sunset from your profile location.

options.description: Shield-style badges for version, licence, build status, stars, downloads and more, each its own image linking to the right page.

style.title: Style
style.description: Large is shields.io's “for the badge” look: taller, in capitals.

color.title: Value colour
color.description: Build status always uses green, amber or red.

options.description: Everyone who has committed to the project as a wall of avatars that pop in one by one, top contributors first.
A warm call to action for sponsors: headline, a short pitch, up to three drawn buttons (GitHub Sponsors, Ko-fi, Open Collective, …) and a beating heart.

buttons.title: Buttons
buttons.description: Drawn into the image; the card links to the first button's URL. URLs default to your account on each platform ({owner} is the repository owner).

backers.title: Backers line
backers.description: A short line under the buttons, e.g. how many people back the work.

options.description: Rolling odometer counters for your key numbers, with an optional year-progress ring.

tiles.title: Tiles
tiles.description: Up to 6 with the ring, 8 without.

options.description: Your most used languages by bytes of code, as an animated donut, bar list or stacked bar.

max.title: Languages shown
max.description: The rest are grouped as Other.

options.description: Hexagonal trophies that unlock in three tiers as your streaks, stars and years on GitHub grow.
Current streak in a burning ring, flanked by your longest run and total contributions, each with its date range.

ranges.title: Date ranges
ranges.description: Show when each streak started and ended.

ring.title: Record ring
ring.description: The ring fills as your current streak approaches your longest.

options.description: Your languages as a donut that draws itself in, with the top language in the centre and a percentage legend.

slices.title: Max slices
slices.description: Smaller languages are grouped as Other.

options.description: Your year, wrapped: total contributions, busiest month, best day, favourite weekday and more, over a monthly bar chart.

facts.title: Highlights
facts.description: Up to six, shown in a 3 × 2 grid.

pace.title: Pace & comparison
pace.description: Projected total and change against last year.

options.description: Your follower count on a rolling counter with a progress bar towards the next milestone.

ladder.title: Milestone ladder
ladder.description: Small markers for the milestones around you.

options.description: Rolling counters for stars, forks, issues, pull requests and contributors, each with a tiny trend, plus an issue-health ring.

tiles.title: Tiles
tiles.description: Up to 6 with the ring, 8 without.

ring.title: Health ring
ring.description: Share of issues closed, with pull requests merged as an inner ring.

options.description: A compact health check: build status with a live pulse, last commit, latest release, issue and pull request balance, and the licence.
Weekly, monthly or all-time downloads from npm, PyPI or crates.io on a rolling counter, with a year-long sparkline and the month-on-month trend.

registry.title: Registry
registry.description: Package names come from the project settings.

options.description: Your last 12 months as an animated heatmap with a scanning beam, best-day callout and weekly totals.
Your recent contributions drawn as an ECG trace, one heartbeat per day, with a glowing pulse running along it.

label.title: Label
label.description: {days} is replaced with the window length.

bpm.title: BPM tile
bpm.description: Average contributions per week, shown as a heart rate.

options.description: Your last 12 months as an isometric city of contribution towers, slowly turning in an animated GIF.
A 24-hour radial clock of when you commit, with your chronotype and busiest weekday.

weekdays.title: Weekday strip
weekdays.description: Contributions per weekday next to the clock.

summary.title: Summary line
summary.description: Chronotype, peak hour and daily average.

options.description: Your years on GitHub as a timeline: contributions per year above the axis, repositories you started below.

years.title: Years
years.description: Most recent years to show; older ones are left out.

options.description: Your latest public GitHub activity on a split-flap departure board that clatters into place.

rows.title: Rows
rows.description: Empty slots stay blank when there is less activity.

clock.title: Clock and handle
clock.description: Build time and your GitHub handle in the corner.

flaps.title: Flap animation
flaps.description: Letters scramble and flip into place.

options.description: Weekly contributions as a smooth area chart that draws itself on, with your average and peak week marked.

points.title: Week dots
points.description: Dots on each week (12 and 26 week ranges).

options.description: Contributions per day of the week as rising bars, with your busiest day lit up.
A scanner drone glides over your contribution graph, harvesting every lit cell into a running tally before the grid regrows.
Cumulative stars over time as a chart that draws itself on, with milestone flags and the stars gained this month.

milestones.title: Milestone flags
milestones.description: Marks when the project crossed 100, 500, 1k, 5k … stars.

options.description: A year of weekly commits as growing bars, a heat strip or a line, with the busiest week called out and the latest commit underneath.

last.title: Latest commit
last.description: Message, short hash and time of the newest commit.

options.description: Spotlights the project you are pushing to right now, with an animated git graph and the last 30 days of activity.

repo.title: Repository
repo.description: Leave empty to always show the repository you pushed to most recently.

sparkline.title: Activity sparkline
sparkline.description: Your contributions over the last 30 days.

progress.title: Lifetime bar
progress.description: How long the repository has existed, from first commit to now.

options.description: One repository as a polished card with its description, language and stars, framed by a running accent light.

index.title: Position
index.description: Which pinned repository, or rank by stars.

options.description: Your best or most recently pushed repositories with descriptions, languages and rolling star counters.

hideProfile.title: Hide profile README repo
hideProfile.description: Skips the repository named after your username.

options.description: A timeline of the versions you shipped most recently, with tag pills, repositories and how long ago each landed.

names.title: Release titles
names.description: Show the release title under the repository when it differs from the tag.

repos.title: Only these repositories
repos.description: Leave empty to include every repository.

options.description: The newest articles from your blog's RSS or Atom feed, with dates and short summaries, refreshed on every build.

feed.title: Feed URL
feed.description: RSS or Atom; fetched by the GitHub Action on every build.

link.title: Card link
link.description: Images can only link as a whole, so the card opens this page.

options.description: Your latest releases on a timeline: version pills, dates, a line or two of release notes and a pulsing marker on the newest one.

kinds.title: Release kind tags
kinds.description: Marks each version as major, minor or patch.

options.description: Milestones as progress rows with status chips, issue counts and due dates, from GitHub milestones or a list you write.

source.title: Source
source.description: Automatic uses the repository's open milestones when there are any, otherwise your list.

options.description: Today at a glance: the date, the moon phase, local weather, the year so far and a quote of the day.

label.title: Label
label.description: Your city from the profile is appended.

weather.title: Weather
weather.description: Current conditions for the location in your profile.

quote.title: Quote of the day
quote.description: A different quote from the list each day.

options.description: A large typographic quote with attribution; add several and it cross-fades through them on a loop.

rotate.title: Rotate through quotes
rotate.description: Cross-fades through every quote in the list; off shows only the first.

options.description: Free-form Markdown or HTML written straight into your README, with live placeholders like {name} and {followers}.

text.title: Markdown
text.description: Emitted verbatim into the README; the row's alignment applies. Placeholders: {name} {login} {city} {company} {role} {year} {followers} {stars} {repos} {streak} {contributions} {project} {repo} {tagline} {version} {license} {forks} {contributors} {npm} {pypi} {crate} {owner}

options.description: A terminal that types your install command, cycling through package-manager tabs, with a copy button and an optional quick-start line.

managers.title: Package managers
managers.description: One tab each, typed in turn. Package names come from the project settings and fall back to the repository name.

quickStart.title: Quick-start line
quickStart.description: A follow-up command such as `npx {npm} init`.

quickStartCmd.title: Quick-start command
quickStartCmd.description: Same command on every tab. Placeholders: {npm} {pypi} {crate} {bin} {repo}.

custom.title: Custom commands
custom.description: Shown as extra tabs when Custom is ticked. An entry labelled like a ticked manager (npm, pip, …) replaces that tab's command.

options.description: A syntax-highlighted code card with a file tab, line numbers, highlighted lines and a line-by-line reveal: perfect for a usage example.

code.title: Code
code.description: Placeholders: {npm} {pypi} {crate} {bin} {repo} {project} {version}. Up to 36 rows are shown.

highlight.title: Highlight lines
highlight.description: Line numbers or ranges to emphasise.

options.description: Your project's highlights as a two- or three-column grid of icon tiles, titles and short descriptions, revealed one by one.

icon.title: Icon
icon.description: A line glyph (bolt, sparkle, code, globe, …) or a brand icon.

options.description: A markdown table of contents with links to your README's sections, numbered or bulleted, with optional sub-entries.

title.title: Heading
title.description: Markdown, e.g. `## Contents` or `**On this page**`. Leave empty for just the list.

entries.title: Entries
entries.description: Anchors default to GitHub's heading slug, so `## Getting started` becomes #getting-started.

options.description: A thin animated separator between sections: comet, pulse, wave, dashes or a fading line.
Rolling waves, a date barcode and a build stamp that proves the profile is alive.

stamp.title: Build stamp
stamp.description: Date, time, run number and data source.

credit.title: Made with Readme Studio
credit.description: A small credit line, and the footer links to Readme Studio. Thank you!

options.description: A slim section title with an eyebrow label and an animated hairline, for giving your README a clear structure.

icon.title: Icon
icon.description: Optional; a brand icon or a line glyph (rocket, code, book, star…).

card.title: Card background
card.description: Off blends the heading into the page.
